zh: 他表明我们都知道我们有热量饥饿，显然，我们都知道这一点，但你的身体也有一种专门针对蛋白质的饥饿，因为你的身体知道你需要蛋白质来做诸如构建骨骼之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以如果你想一想，如果你的饮食以加工食品为主，就像我几乎一生都是这样，你的身体需要一定量的蛋白质。

zh: 如果你给人们低蛋白质食物，为了满足身体对蛋白质本身的潜在饥饿，他们会吃更多这种食物。

zh: 加工食品和超加工食品在这里发生了很多像这样的因素。

zh: 我在书中详细介绍了这些，这解释了为什么它会导致我们如此大量地过度饮食，以及为什么它如此深刻地破坏我们的饱腹感、满足感，那种吃饱了不想要更多的感觉。

en: And that's why I think this is almost as much of an economic story as a health story, because you do have these food companies processing food, manufacturing food in a way that make people not feel full and eat as much as possible.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以这是一个大产业。

en: Who's a brilliant expert on hunger at Drexel University in Philly, been researching this for 40 years.

speaker: Unknown
en: He said, these new weight loss drugs are an artificial solution to an artificial problem, right?
zh: 他说,这些新的减肥药是对一个人为问题的人为解决方案,对吧?

en: And what's your experience been like in the year and five months that you've used Ozempic?
zh: 在你使用 Ozempic 的一年零五个月里,你的体验是怎样的?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而 GLP-1 基本上是你身体的自然信号在说,嘿伙计,你吃够了,别吃了,对吧?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这些药物所做的是给你注射一种人工合成的 GLP-1 副本,它不是只停留几分钟,而是在你的系统中停留整整一周,这产生了这种不可思议的效果。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这是一个深刻的科学突破。

speaker: Unknown

en: It's why I went from eating...

zh: 服用它的普通人在一年内减掉体重的 21%。

zh: 目前有两百多种此类药物正在研发中。

zh: 因为我们知道有超过四十种肠道激素会影响食欲。

en: Yeah, obesity.

en: Maybe your uncle died of a heart attack.

speaker: Unknown

en: He was taking fistfuls of pills every morning.
zh: 他每天早上都要一把一把地吃药。

speaker: Unknown
en: He started to take Manjaro.
zh: 他开始服用 Manjaro。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, he was getting a compounded version from China, like you say.
zh: 实际上，他就像你说的那样，从中国获得的是复方版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lost an enormous amount of weight, came off all his pills, all his medical conditions went into reverse.
zh: 减掉了大量的体重，停掉了所有的药，所有的医疗状况都逆转了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now he walks his dog over the Golden Gate Bridge every day.
zh: 现在他每天带着狗走过金门大桥。

speaker: Unknown
en: And said to me, I feel like I'm going to enjoy my retirement.
zh: 他对我说，我觉得我要享受我的退休生活了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, everyone who knows Jeff looks at him and goes, whoa, what happened to Jeff, right?
zh: 现在，每个认识 Jeff 的人看着他都 会说，哇，Jeff 怎么了，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: He looks completely different.
zh: 他看起来完全不同了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the reasons there's these shortages is that everyone then becomes a walking ad.
zh: 所以出现这些短缺的原因之一就是每个人都变成了活广告。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so demand produces demand, produces demand, produces demand in this cascading effect.
zh: 所以需求产生需求，产生需求，产生需求，产生这种级联效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: So although they have been, Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly, the companies that make these drugs, have been massively, to be fair to them, expanding production.
zh: 尽管它们……诺和诺德和礼来，这些制造药物的公司，已经大规模地，公平地说，在扩大生产。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, they want to, they want to make the money.
zh: 当然，他们想，他们想赚钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're racing to get to a finishing line that's just getting further and further away because the more they race, the more people want it, right?
zh: 他们正奔向一条终点线，但这终点线正变得越来越远，因为他们越是奔跑，人们就越想要，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So lots of companies are producing compounded copies of these drugs.
zh: 所以很多公司正在生产这些药物的复方仿制品。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's inherently risks in that.
zh: 这其中存在固有的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not made in FDA labs.
zh: 它们不是在 FDA 实验室制造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In Austria recently, there was a big problem where people bought what they thought was compounded semaglutides, the active component of these drugs.
zh: 最近在奥地利，有一个大问题，人们买了他们认为是复方 semaglutides 的东西，这是这些药物的活性成分。

speaker: Unknown
en: They weren't.
zh: 它们不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: They went into comas.
zh: 他们陷入了昏迷。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were horribly injured.
zh: 他们受了重伤。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's an inherent risk in compounded versions for obvious reasons.
zh: 复方版本存在固有风险，原因显而易见。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I understand why people are doing it, right?
zh: 但我理解人们为什么这样做，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, there's a tremendous complexity.
zh: 所以是的，这里有巨大的复杂性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you're right that big pharma will be pressuring to close those loopholes pretty soon.
zh: 我认为你是对的，大型制药公司将很快施压关闭这些漏洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, they're already sending out lawyers' letters to health spas.
zh: 我的意思是，他们已经在向健康水疗中心发出律师函了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if that happens, I mean, you could abruptly have people thrown off the medicine, whereas they can afford the compounded drug.
zh: 如果发生这种情况，我的意思是，人们可能会突然被断药，而他们还负担得起复方药物。

speaker: Unknown
en: They cannot afford $1,300 a month.
zh: 他们负担不起每月 1300 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what happens if you get abruptly tossed off the drug?
zh: 所以如果你突然被断药会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's a really important question.
zh: 嗯，这是一个非常重要的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want to explain what the drug companies say, and I want to explain why they're probably right, but we need to take it with a small pinch of salt.
zh: 所以我想解释一下制药公司的说法，我想解释为什么他们可能是对的，但我们需要对此持一点保留态度。

speaker: Unknown
en: What the drug companies say is these drugs are like statins or blood pressure meds.
zh: 制药公司的说法是，这些药物就像他汀类药物或降压药。

speaker: Unknown
en: They work for as long as you take them, and when you stop taking them, they stop working.
zh: 只要你服用它们，它们就起作用，当你停止服用时，它们就停止工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you regain the weight pretty rapidly.
zh: 所以你会很快恢复体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they have funded a study that seems to demonstrate this.
zh: 他们资助了一项似乎证明了这一点的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The vast majority of people regain the vast majority of their weight within a year.
zh: 绝大多数人在一年内恢复了绝大多数体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a small pinch of salt in that, in that of course they have a vested interest in telling us that we have to take them forever because they make money forever.
zh: 对此有一点保留意见，那就是当然他们有既得利益告诉我们要永远服用，因为他们永远赚钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: There do seem anecdotally to be some people who take them for a shorter period, use them to radically change their habits, and then seem to stay at a lower weight, although I suspect they're a minority.
zh: 从轶事上看，确实似乎有一些人服用它们的时间较短，利用它们来彻底改变他们的习惯，然后似乎保持在较低的体重，尽管我怀疑他们是少数。

speaker: Unknown
en: There'll be more research on this soon.
zh: 不久将会有更多关于这方面的研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, if you're thrown off, you'll almost certainly regain the weight.
zh: 但是是的，如果你被停药，你几乎肯定会恢复体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right and that could be a very big issue as we see again these opposing forces sort of try to jockey for position here as this drug takes off.
zh: 是的，这可能是一个非常大的问题，因为我们再次看到这些对立的力量在这里试图争夺位置，随着这种药物的兴起。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be worse than that.
zh: 情况可能比那更糟。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know and there's a lot of things we don't know about these drugs.
zh: 我们不知道，而且关于这些药物有很多我们不知道的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is so we know if you gained a load of weight now and then went on a diet and lost weight and it just through calorie restriction and exercise so not using these drugs
zh: 一个是我们知道，如果你现在增加了很多体重，然后节食减肥，并且只是通过热量限制和运动，所以不使用这些药物

speaker: Unknown
en: We know that slows down your metabolism over time.
zh: 我们知道随着时间的推移这会减慢你的新陈代谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes it harder to keep weight off, right?
zh: 这使得保持体重下降变得更难，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you yo-yo diet, if you gain weight, lose weight, gain weight, lose weight, it can really wreck your metabolism so you actually burn calories very slowly.
zh: 如果你进行溜溜球式节食，如果你增加体重，减轻体重，增加体重，减轻体重，它真的会破坏你的新陈代谢，以至于你实际上燃烧卡路里非常慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know if taking these drugs and then coming off them slows down your metabolism.
zh: 我们不知道服用这些药物然后停药是否会减慢你的新陈代谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably does.
zh: 可能会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most other forms of weight loss do.
zh: 大多数其他形式的减肥都会。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, all other forms of weight loss do.
zh: 事实上，所有其他形式的减肥都会。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's another concern as well.
zh: 所以这也是另一个担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could you actually end up fatter than you were if you hadn't taken the drug?
zh: 如果你没有服用这种药物，你最终是否可能比以前更胖？

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know, but it's a concern.
zh: 我们不知道，但这令人担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things that I found so interesting in your book was this concept of a set point that your body basically figures out the weight that you are, the weight that you should be.
zh: 在你的书中，我发现非常有趣的一件事是设定点的概念，你的身体基本上弄清楚你的体重，你应该有的体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you try to move too far off of it, at least, you know, in terms of the negative, it will try to bring you back up to that set point of weight.
zh: 如果你试图偏离它太远，至少，你知道，在负面方面，它会试图让你回到那个体重设定点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, this is really interesting because there's the way people used to think about this in the 60s and 70s and there's the way we understand it now.
zh: 嗯，这真的很有趣，因为人们在 60 年代和 70 年代以前对这种方式的看法，以及我们现在理解的方式之间有区别。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in the 60s and 70s, scientists thought that your weight was basically set from birth or even in utero, that basically from when you're born, you have a certain fat percentage that's kind of innate to you, right?
zh: 所以在 60 年代和 70 年代，科学家认为你的体重基本上是从出生起甚至在子宫内就设定了的，基本上从你出生的时候起，你就有某种对你来说是天生的脂肪百分比，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So think about your temperature set point as an analogy.
zh: 所以把你的温度设定点作为一个类比来思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a natural set body temperature.
zh: 我们有一个自然的设定体温。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you go higher than that, your body works very hard to bring it down.
zh: 如果你高于那个温度，你的身体会非常努力地把它降下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes you sweat.
zh: 它让你出汗。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes you really want to get into the shade.
zh: 它让你真的很想进入阴凉处。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you go lower than that, your body works really hard to bring it up.
zh: 如果你低于那个温度，你的身体会非常努力地把它升起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes you shiver.
zh: 它让你发抖。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes you seek warmth.
zh: 它让你寻找温暖。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was thought that so it's very hard to stay out.
zh: 人们认为所以很难保持在外。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, you can't stay outside your safe temperature level, your temperature set point for very long, right?
zh: 基本上，你不能在安全的温度水平之外，你的温度设定点之外停留很长时间，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Your body really works to keep you there.
zh: 你的身体非常努力地让你保持在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you do stay out of it for long, you get very unwell.
zh: 如果你在那之外停留太久，你会变得非常不舒服。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was thought that there was something similar with your weight, that you had an innate set point that just sort of regulated.
zh: 所以人们认为你的体重也有类似的东西，你有一个天生的设定点，只是某种程度上的调节。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could go a little bit above or a little bit below, but it was basically set and regulated.
zh: 你可以稍微高一点或稍微低一点，但它基本上是设定和调节的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the obesity crisis happened, mainly starting in the early 1980s, late 70s, early 80s when I was born.
zh: 然后肥胖危机发生了，主要是在 1980 年代早期，70 年代后期，80 年代早期，当我出生的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not blaming myself.
zh: 我不是在责怪自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not like Damien in The Omen, couldn't cause it.
zh: 我不像《凶兆》里的 Damien，我无法造成它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that seemed to blow set point theory up, right?
zh: 这似乎推翻了设定点理论，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, what's going on?
zh: 那么，发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's set, if it's innate and biological,
zh: 如果它是设定的，如果它是天生的和生物性的，

speaker: Unknown
en: How come it changed so much so quickly?
zh: 为什么它变化得如此之快如此之多？

speaker: Unknown
en: But what scientists realized, this is contested, but I think it's quite persuasive, is actually what happens is you do have an innate set point, but as you gain weight, your set point rises.
zh: 但科学家们意识到了——这一点虽然有争议，但我认为它很有说服力——实际上发生的情况是，你确实有一个先天设定点，但随着你的体重增加，你的设定点也会上升。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is really important for understanding why the alternative to these drugs, diet and exercise, does not produce sustained weight loss for about 85% of people who try it.
zh: 这对于理解为什么这些药物的替代方案——即饮食和运动——对于约 85% 的尝试者来说无法产生持续的体重减轻，这一点非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's say that you now gained 40 pounds.
zh: 所以假设你现在体重增加了 40 磅。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you try to lose that 40 pounds through calorie restriction and exercise.
zh: 你试图通过限制卡路里和运动来减掉这 40 磅。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because your innate set point has risen, your brain is trying to hold you at that higher weight.
zh: 因为你的先天设定点已经上升，你的大脑正试图让你保持在那个更高的体重上。

speaker: Unknown
en: All sorts of physical and biological changes will happen in your brain and your body to try to stop you going down.
zh: 你的大脑和身体里会发生各种各样的生理和生物变化，试图阻止你的体重下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will slow your metabolism down so you burn calories more slowly.
zh: 它会减慢你的新陈代谢，这样你燃烧卡路里的速度就会变慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll make you crave more sugary, salty foods.
zh: 它会让你更渴望高糖、高盐的食物。

speaker: Unknown
en: All sorts of changes happen.
zh: 各种各样的变化都会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's lots of evidence for that, overwhelming evidence about metabolic slowdown, for example.
zh: 这方面有很多证据，例如关于新陈代谢减慢就有压倒性的证据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember when I first learned that, thinking, well, that can't be true.
zh: 我记得当我第一次了解到这一点时，我想，嗯，这不可能是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because why, obesity is really bad for your health.
zh: 因为为什么，肥胖真的对你的健康有害。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would evolution endow us with the desire to hold onto, or biological mechanisms to hold onto obesity, given that obesity is so bad for us, it's so maladaptive, it doesn't make sense to me.
zh: 既然肥胖对我们如此不利，它是如此的不适应，进化为什么会赋予我们保持肥胖的欲望，或者保持肥胖的生物机制，这对我来说说不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was explained to me by Professor Michael Lowe, who I mentioned before at Drexel.
zh: 德雷塞尔大学 的 Michael Lowe 教授向我解释了这一点，我之前提到过他。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best way of thinking about this, I think, which is you've got to think about the circumstances where human beings evolved.
zh: 我认为思考这个问题最好的方式是，你必须考虑人类进化的环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the circumstances where human beings evolved,
zh: 在人类进化的环境中，

speaker: Unknown
en: The situation we live in now essentially never happened or vanishingly rarely, which is where you have...
zh: 我们现在生活的处境基本上从未发生过，或者极其罕见，那就是你周围有……

speaker: Unknown
en: Infinite, abundant calories all around you, far more than you could consume, and they last your whole life, right?
zh: 无限的、丰富的卡路里，远远超过你能消耗的量，而且它们伴随你一生，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That just never happened.
zh: 这从未发生过。

speaker: Unknown
en: So evolution did not prepare us for that scenario.
zh: 所以进化并没有让我们为那种情况做好准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: The scenario that did happen quite frequently that evolution did prepare us for is the exact opposite, famine.
zh: 进化确实让我们做好准备的、且相当频繁发生的情况恰恰相反，那就是饥荒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Famine was very common, right?
zh: 饥荒非常普遍，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: In the circumstances where human beings evolved, it was quite likely there would be a famine in your lifetime.
zh: 在人类进化的环境中，在你的一生中很有可能发生一次饥荒。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about it in that context, it makes perfect sense that if you gain weight, your body fights to hold on to the weight, right?
zh: 如果在那个背景下思考，如果你体重增加，你的身体会努力保持体重，这就完全说得通，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: If there's a famine, the fattest man at the start is the last man standing, right?
zh: 如果发生饥荒，开始时最胖的人是最后站着的人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a famine.
zh: 发生了一场饥荒。

speaker: Unknown
en: The version of me from three years ago is going to still be alive at the end, whereas Timothee Chalamet will die in week one, right?
zh: 三年前的我会活到最后，而 Timothee Chalamet 会在第一周就死掉，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll cry over his body, but he'll bury him and we'll have to move on, right?
zh: 我会为了他的尸体哭泣，但他会埋葬他，我们只能继续前行，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Rest in peace.
zh: 安息吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 确实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rest in peace, Timothee Chalamet.
zh: 安息吧，Timothee Chalamet。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 确实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Big Tim.
zh: Big Tim。

speaker: Unknown
en: This set point, this innate set point is preparing us for a famine that now is never going to come, right?
zh: 这个设定点，这个先天设定点正在为我们准备一场永远不会到来的饥荒，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So that explains why diets don't work.
zh: 所以这解释了为什么节食不起作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also explains one theory, although this is significantly more contentious.
zh: 它还解释了一种理论，尽管这一点争议要大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a huge debate about what these drugs, so we now know these drugs are primarily working not on your gut, but on your brain.
zh: 关于这些药物有巨大的争论，所以我们要知道这些药物主要不是作用于你的肠道，而是作用于你的大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have GLP-1 receptors, not just in your gut, but in your brain.
zh: 你的肠道和大脑中都有 GLP-1 受体。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're profoundly changing our brains.
zh: 它们在深刻地改变我们的大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: From interviewing the cutting edge neuroscientists as I did for my book, this is very clear.
zh: 正如我为我的书采访那些前沿神经科学家时所了解到的，这一点非常清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's so disconcerting to interview the leading neuroscientists and you say to them, well, what is it doing to my brain?
zh: 采访顶尖的神经科学家非常令人不安，你对他们说，嗯，它对我的大脑在做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they kind of go, yeah, come back and ask us in a few years, we don't really know.
zh: 他们有点像那样说，是啊，过几年再来问我们，我们真的不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: But one theory about what it may be doing to the brain is it may be lowering your biological set point.
zh: 但关于它可能对大脑做什么的一种理论是，它可能正在降低你的生物设定点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The equivalent of, this is a very crude analogy, I suspect the scientists I interviewed would think it was overly crude, but it's a bit like taking your set point, resetting your iPhone to the factory settings, right?
zh: 相当于——这是一个非常粗略的类比，我怀疑我采访的科学家会认为这太粗略了——但这有点像把你的设定点，把你的 iPhone 重置为出厂设置，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It lowers your set point for the duration that you take the drugs.
zh: 在你服用药物的期间，它会降低你的设定点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So again, you see, the debate about what causes obesity is intimately related to the debate about how these drugs work in all sorts of fascinating ways.
zh: 所以你看，再次看到，关于什么导致肥胖的辩论与关于这些药物如何工作的辩论有着各种各样迷人的方式紧密相关。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you mentioned brain chemistry.
zh: 你提到了大脑化学。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's something that I definitely want to talk about.
zh: 这绝对是我想要谈论的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just want to talk about whether kids should be taking these drugs.
zh: 我只是想谈谈孩子们是否应该服用这些药物。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the kids, the US at least, has approved kids as young as 12 taking these drugs.
zh: 我认为孩子们，美国至少，已经批准低至 12 岁的孩子服用这些药物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're going to do that on the other side of this break, back right after this.
zh: 我们将在这次间歇的另一侧进行，马上就回来。

en: This episode is brought to you by DeepL.
